title: MEN'S BASKETBALL | Chris Jans Postgame Radio Interview vs. UCF - 11/17/26
text: gutsy effort by your team, especially the second half of the game. What'd you talk to them about in the locker room? >> A lot. A lot. I was proud of them for an early season road victory. Um I didn't tell them this, but personally, I felt like, and it's kind of crazy to say, but on my family group thread, it was this is a must-win for us. I just felt like after the last outing that we needed to regain some confidence uh going forward. Uh I knew it was going to be hard on the road against a Big 12 appointed opponent that obviously has some talent and um do a really good job who made the NCA tournament last year. Um but I thought we had a bunch of guys that really stepped up. I the first thing that I shouted out was was TJ Simpkins coming off the bench basically cold um and and the one to get fouled and and knocked him down. I thought that was a big turning point in the game. Obviously King Grace going 14 for 14 from the free throw line and you know made some big plays. I thought as a team the things that stood out were uh holding one to six points after basically he you know scored half their points in the first half with 20. He's a heck of a player. And then obviously the rebounding differential uh you know as the game wore on you know that the rebounding uh difference started to grow and that was a big big deal for us. And then of course, you know, Hubard had his a dagger three that uh obviously we almost spoiled it by not closing it out, but that was a big big basket when we needed it. >> So, let's talk about your strategy against Dior Johnson in the second half of the game. From here, it looked like I know it's team defense, but it's King Grace and it's Tomas Bong on him most of the second half. Was there an adjustment there? What led to being able to shut him down in the second half? Yeah, we played it more straight in the first half. um just to get a feel for it. And we had practiced some possible adjustments heading into the game. And basically it was, you know, every time he was one pass away, you know, face guard him and then if he was going to drive the basketball to his right hand and and you were in that gap, no, no matter what, unless it was number 24, you were going to close that gap and make him kick it and just try to, you know, and I I was telling text going into the game, you know, prep-wise, I'm like, we can't let one beat us. like and certainly uh he he reminded me of that of halftime, you know, so we had to make some changes on what we were doing with him and I'm really glad that he reminded me of that and and we pulled the trigger and our guys more importantly did a really good job of of executing the game plan in the second half when we we went to an adjustment that way. >> I talked to King about this right after the game, but you last year you had to lean so heavily on Josh to score for you. They took him away, limited his touches and shot opportunities in the first half tonight. R.J. steps up for you in a big way. King gets to the free throw line, gives you some offense. Tristan's huge in the five spot. How much more confident is this group or how much more confident do you feel knowing that if they're trying to take Josh away, you've got other people who can step up and provide some offense? >> Yeah, I've been uh I I'm on record many times saying how much I enjoy um coaching this group of of young people. They're um great human beings. They're awesome kids. They have a really good mindset coming in uh to practice every day and I truly believe that they they like each other and when you have that and you can handle some adversity and we'll have a lot more uh and continue to stick together that that stuff will show up in close games. It'll show up and and you'll win some close games and obviously we're in the infant stages of a marathon um basketball season. But um in terms of just Josh how he feels. I mean that's more probably for him. But I I'd imagine uh he feels like there's more help and there's a big load off his shoulders and you know last year with with him having 13 on 11 shots we probably don't don't win this game. But um and again there I go again. I'm about done talking about last year just so you know. Um we're we're what four four five games into it now. I think that's enough to put that season to to rest. Your fiveman tonight was really good and Tristan was really good against Jackson State. To see him come out tonight and really assert himself in the paint. Is he starting to turn a corner? He's he's growing out a freshy you think a little bit. >> Uh let's not go there. Not quite yet. But you know, we were celebrating in there and uh he pushed uh one of the other players and jarred him pretty good and and my comment was quit fouling. you [laughter] know, and everyone broke up and obviously he fouls way too much and we've got to figure that out. But, um, he was a big boost for us. I mean, 16 and 11 on the road in his first two road games, six offensive rebounds and certainly who knows what his line would have been if, uh, you know, he had hadn't been plagued with with foul trouble. >> Well, and RJ, there was a point early in the second half where he just looked like he took it on himself and said, "I'm going to do everything I can to make sure we get the lead back here early." I keep being impressed by his physicality, his different ways of scoring. I What's he adding to your team? >> Well, again, it gets Hubba off the ball. Uh he's got that big wide frame. He's still learning how to use it at this level if we're being honest. I mean, he was six for 14, so not super efficient. Four for six from the line, but he had five assists, seven rebounds, 18 points, and played, you know, almost 35 minutes a game. And once he continues to to work on his game and and understand where his spots are around the paint, it's an added, you know, uh, luxury for us when you got a big bully point guard that can get downhill and and score in the paint and, uh, you know, not just play traditionally on the perimeter that way, but and his defense is coming. He's starting to figure out how important it is. And he's got that length and and that size. And obviously, he was a he was really, really good tonight. Like you mentioned, we really needed a a spurt. Um, and I thought he provided it. You've got now three more of these away from home before you get to come back home for that Georgia Tech game. What do you hope your guys learn from an experience like this that they can take with them to Jackson and then on to the Bahamas? >> Well, we learned a lot against Xavier about just quality of play all the time, never taking your foot off the gas. Um, just got to be locked in. And then we also learned that, you know, when you're down double digits, it it's a long way from home. And and we just didn't know how to come back. we didn't know not to foul and, you know, looking for the eight-point shot and watching film and trying to learn from that game was was some lessons. And um and then tonight, you know, we had to hold him off and and make some late game situations and we fouled the the first time when they had it on purpose. I told Thomas that two got it to foul him uh because of his free throw numbers and he did a really good job of that. And then the second time we decided not to, especially after they threw the ball in and it looked like it was maybe going to be a turnover. But, um, you know, learning how to win, learning how to play in in close games, which this is the first one that we've had all year long and, uh, I'd imagine we'll have a whole bunch of them before the season's over. >> Congratulations. It'll be a good plane ride home. Thanks for coming out. >> It will. Thank you, Hill State. >> That is Chris Jans. The state wins at 8683 over UCF to get to 4-1 on the
